I'm a 58-year-old farmer in Quzhou County with primary schooling and 40 years of working this land. My family has 4 mouths to feed, and some of them work off-farm, so I can't always count on having enough hands around. I've got about 30 mu total. Most of it goes to wheat and corn because that's what works here — the double crop keeps food on the table. I also keep about 5 mu of stevia because there's a buyer who comes by for it, and it pays decent when the corn price is low.

**Winter wheat (24 mu):**
I plant wheat in early October, around the same time as my neighbors. I've been using the same wheat variety for a few years now — it's reliable, and the seed costs about 25 yuan per mu. I put down roughly 15 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, then topdress with urea at jointing if the wheat looks a bit yellow. Usually that's about 10 kg more per mu. For watering, I irrigate about 3 times: once before winter if it's too dry, once at jointing around Qingming, and once at grain filling in May. Pumping water costs money, so I don't water more than I have to, but you can't skip jointing — that's when the yield is made. I expect maybe 450 kg per mu if the weather cooperates, which is about what I got last year.

**Summer maize (24 mu, same land after wheat):**
The window between wheat harvest and corn planting is tight — sometimes only a few days. I don't do deep tillage, just turn the stubble under quickly and plant by hand or hire a machine if my nephew is around with his. I plant hybrid corn seed, costs about 35 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I put down about 15 kg of compound fertilizer at planting, and that's usually it for corn — it grows fast and the heat helps. If it stays dry in July, I'll irrigate once or maybe twice, but corn doesn't need as much water as wheat. I hire a couple of days of labor for planting because it's too much for just me and my wife when the clock is ticking. I figure on about 500 kg per mu, maybe a bit less if it's a dry summer.

**Stevia (6 mu):**
I put stevia on the better-drained patch near the road. I plant seedlings in late April. Stevia doesn't need much nitrogen — maybe 8 kg per mu total, and I put it all down at planting. I water it twice, once after transplanting and once in June if there's no rain. I harvest once in late July or early August when the leaves are sweetest. I don't use much pesticide on it, just a herbicide spray early on. I expect about 200 kg of dry leaves per mu, which is decent money for the space.

**Costs and thinking:**
This year I'm being careful with money because fertilizer prices went up again. I'm not cutting back too much — I'd rather put a bit too much than too little, because a bad yield hurts worse than spending a few extra yuan. But I'm not trying anything fancy either. My neighbor tried some new wheat variety last year and had trouble with disease, so I'm sticking with what I know. My son works in the factory in town, so he sends some money home, which helps with buying inputs, but I still watch every yuan. The stevia gives me a bit of cash in summer before the corn comes in, which helps with liquidity. All told, I'll spend about 12,000 yuan on seeds, fertilizer, water, and hired labor for the year. That's a lot, but I need to keep the land producing.
